Currently the "checking your bits" page is 738kB. The Javascript won't start until the entire (uncacheable) page is downloaded, which takes about 3 seconds for me (increasing the total wait from 5 to 8 seconds), so it could use some slimming down.

Almost all of that size is due to CSS and files that CloudFlare inlined into the CSS as data: URLs:

  • 149kB - CSS apparently copied from bootstrap.css and Voat.css
  • 26kB - inlined copy of fonts/glyphicons-halflings-regular.eot
  • 31kB - inlined copy of fonts/glyphicons-halflings-regular.woff
  • 59kB - inlined copy of fonts/glyphicons-halflings-regular.ttf
  • 394kB - 14 inlined copies of Graphics/WVSprite.png
  • 66kB - 9 inlined copies of Graphics/Light-SpriteSheet.png
  • 13kB - actual content

Very little of the CSS included is actually used in the page - in particular, none of the sprite images or fonts seem to be used. There are programs that will remove unused CSS selectors from a file, but even just manually removing the glyphicons and sprites stuff would be a huge improvement.

394kB - 14 inlined copies of Graphics/WVSprite.png

Is a single, repeated image downloaded 14 times? Is that really how the web works?

Not in general. In the original file, the CSS is like

.whoaverse_padded { background: url( /Graphics/WVSprite.png ) 0 0; height: 44px; width: 125px; }
.nsfw-thumb { background: url( /Graphics/WVSprite.png ) 0 -176px; height: 70px; width: 70px; }
.pattern-welcome { background: url( /Graphics/WVSprite.png ) 0 -246px; height: 128px; width: 128px; } ...

which would lead to the file being downloaded only once and cached. However, CloudFlare converts each reference to an inline data: URL since everything has to be in a single .html file. This results in the data being repeated:

.whoaverse_padded { background: url(data:image/png;charset=binary;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAAN...(28 kB of base64-encoded image data)) 0 0; height: 44px; width: 125px; }
.nsfw-thumb { background: url(data:image/png;charset=binary;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAAN...(28 kB of base64-encoded image data)) 0 -176px; height: 70px; width: 70px; }
.pattern-welcome { background: url(data:image/png;charset=binary;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAAN...(28 kB of base64-encoded image data)) 0 -246px; height: 128px; width: 128px; } ...
